headline: REA Gives Agents a Forensic Workbench
lede: REA turns reverse engineering into a coordinated agent workflow. It connects coding assistants and terminal commands to local tools such as Ghidra, Hopper, Binwalk, and JADX, returning evidence, relationships, limitations, and unknowns alongside its conclusions.

headline: AnyPS5 Relinks Console Code for Desktop Systems
lede: AnyPS5 attacks platform boundaries at the executable level. Its relinker translates PlayStation 5 binaries for Linux and Windows, while native PRX libraries and a SPIR-V shader recompiler pursue practical compatibility without an emulation layer.

headline: ArtCraft Turns Generative Media Into a Scene
lede: ArtCraft puts composition before generation. Its desktop workspace combines canvas editing, 3D staging, asset kitbashing, and access to image, video, audio, mesh, and world models so creators can iterate on a scene instead of merely prompting one.

headline: Diagram Design Builds Polished SVGs From Plain Language
lede: Diagram Design lays out a repeatable path from request to standalone graphic. An agent selects among 44 diagram types, follows a grid, checks for overlap and clipping, and exports editable HTML and SVG with optional brand colors and fonts.

headline: God’s Eye View Maps a Moving Planet
lede: God’s Eye View pours public telemetry into an explorable 3D globe. Flight transponders, ship beacons, orbital data, and camera feeds become layered visual streams, with cockpit controls, sensor modes, and clear separation between live sources and reconstructed simulation.

headline: PyTorch Keeps Research Flexible at Production Scale
lede: PyTorch connects Python-first experimentation to serious hardware. Dynamic computation, automatic differentiation, GPU backends, and optimization tooling let researchers reshape models quickly while giving production teams a path toward scalable deployment.

headline: AirLLM Streams Giant Models Through Small GPUs
lede: AirLLM treats memory as a scheduling problem rather than a hard limit. It loads model layers from disk or host memory as needed, pairing compression, CPU and Apple Silicon support, and selective expert loading with a Transformers-style interface.

headline: Apollo 11’s Guidance Code Remains Open to Study
lede: The Apollo 11 repository preserves Comanche055 and Luminary099, the assembly programs flown on the Command and Lunar Module guidance computers. Scans, transcription history, metadata, and reproducible compilation keep this software legible as both engineering artifact and primary historical record.
